newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVIA - NOON RADIO HEADLINES - APRIL 9.
newsitem.headline: LATVIA - NOON RADIO HEADLINES - APRIL 9.

text.p: These are the main headlines reported by Latvian state radio on Wednesday at noon. Reuters has not verified these reports and cannot vouch for their accuracy.

- American oil company Amoco says it will unilaterally break its agreement on prospecting for Baltic sea oil if Latvia and Lithuania will not come to terms about their sea border soon, the company's official told Lirhuanian Parliament speaker Vitautas Landbergis in Washington.

- PM Andris Shkele left for an official visit to Sweden. An agreement on the repatriation of illegal immigrants is expected to be signed, which is seen as an important step towards achieving preconditions for visa-free travel between the two countries.

- Economy minister Guntar Krasts is ready to leave his government post if a compromise is not reached in the row over Privatisation Agency management rotation. Krasts earlier said, that he wants to replace all four managers and to choose new people in a competition, which is opposed by PM Andris Shkele.
- Consultative committee of government-forming factions might look into PA management row on April 16.
- Procurators Office says, that investigation has been completed in Lata International credit squandering case.
